name: Willamette Valley AVA
summary: Oregon's largest and best-known wine appellation, containing nested sub-appellations such as the Dundee Hills, Chehalem Mountains and Eola-Amity Hills.

name: Dundee Hills AVA
summary: Sub-appellation lying entirely within the Willamette Valley AVA, home to many of Oregon's earliest Pinot noir plantings. The Oregon Wine Board dates it to 2004; most other sources say 2005.

sources.title: About the Dundee Hills AVA (Oregon Wine Board)

name: Southern Oregon AVA
summary: Appellation established in 2004 on a petition from Earl Jones and Gregory V. Jones of Abacela, so that the Umpqua Valley and Rogue Valley could market themselves jointly. It contains both of those AVAs and their sub-appellations.

name: Umpqua Valley AVA
summary: Douglas County appellation established in 1984, home to HillCrest Vineyard and described as the oldest post-Prohibition wine region in Oregon. It became a sub-appellation of the Southern Oregon AVA in 2004.

name: Rogue Valley AVA
summary: Appellation in Jackson and Josephine counties established in 1991, lying entirely within the Southern Oregon AVA. The Applegate Valley is its only sub-appellation.

name: Applegate Valley AVA
summary: Sub-appellation lying entirely within the Rogue Valley AVA, established in December 2000. Peter Britt's nineteenth-century Valley View vineyard and its 1972 revival by the Wisnovsky family are both tied to the area.

name: McMinnville AVA
summary: Sub-appellation of the Willamette Valley AVA approved in January 2005 on a petition from Kevin Byrd of Youngberg Hill Vineyards.

name: Van Duzer Corridor AVA
summary: Sub-appellation lying entirely within the Willamette Valley AVA, established by a final rule published in December 2018 on a petition from Jeff Havlin of Havlin Vineyard.

name: Walla Walla Valley AVA
summary: Appellation established in 1984 in southeast Washington that extends into the northeastern corner of Oregon, lying entirely within the Columbia Valley AVA.

name: The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater AVA
summary: Sub-appellation of the Walla Walla Valley AVA in Umatilla County, Oregon, established in February 2015 on a petition from Whitman College geologist Kevin Pogue.

sources.title: The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater AVA (Wikipedia)

name: Eola-Amity Hills AVA
summary: Sub-appellation of the Willamette Valley in Polk and Yamhill counties, approved in 2006 on a petition from Russell Raney of Evesham Wood and Ted Casteel of Bethel Heights.

name: Yamhill-Carlton AVA
summary: Sub-appellation lying entirely within the Willamette Valley AVA, established in December 2004 as the Yamhill-Carlton District. The name was shortened in 2010 on a petition from Ken Wright.

name: Ribbon Ridge AVA
summary: Small sub-appellation established in 2005, contained entirely within the Chehalem Mountains AVA in the Willamette Valley.

name: Chehalem Mountains AVA
summary: Sub-appellation lying entirely within the Willamette Valley AVA, established in 2006 on a petition authored by David Adelsheim, Paul Hart and Richard Ponzi. Contains the Ribbon Ridge and Laurelwood District AVAs.

name: Laurelwood District AVA
summary: Established in 2020 within the Chehalem Mountains AVA on a petition from Luisa Ponzi, Maria Ponzi and Kevin Johnson of Dion Vineyards.

name: Tualatin Hills AVA
summary: Appellation in the northernmost part of the Willamette Valley AVA, approved in 2020. Its oldest vineyards include David Hill, the former Charles Coury property.
